subject: landscape-architecture
intro: Landscape architecture turns training in plants, grading and design into paid work shaping parks, campuses, streetscapes and whole regions — and into the planning and conservation offices that guide them.

roles.title: Landscape Architects
roles.entry: Bachelor's or master's degree in landscape architecture
roles.what: Plan and design land areas for projects such as parks and recreational facilities, airports, highways, hospitals, schools, land subdivisions, and commercial, industrial and residential sites.
roles.where: The syllabus is the licensure path: the design process studio and site analysis, planting design and ecology, grading and earthwork in the construction unit, plus the professional practice unit's contracts and ethics prepare you for practice and the LARE.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Develop comprehensive plans and programs for the use of land and physical facilities of jurisdictions such as towns, cities, counties and metropolitan areas.
roles.where: The landscape planning unit — regional planning, cultural and heritage landscapes, GIS for landscape architecture — and the urban design unit's parks, streetscapes and heat-island work are the stock-in-trade of planning departments.

roles.title: Architects, Except Landscape and Naval
roles.what: Plan and design structures such as private residences, office buildings, theaters, factories and other structural property, coordinating drawings, specifications and construction oversight.
roles.where: Shared ground matters here: site analysis and inventory, grading and earthwork, stormwater and green infrastructure from the construction unit, and the practice unit's construction documents make you the collaborator architects reach for on site design.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources so their use does not damage the environment, conducting soil surveys and developing plans to eliminate soil erosion, protect rangelands and advise land managers on conservation practices.
roles.where: The planting design and ecology unit — plant communities, soils and hydrology, ecological restoration — and the landscape planning unit's regional-scale analysis are exactly the ecological literacy this work runs on.
